points.description: Names a first distinct process that moves substances across the cell membrane and describes how it works correctly, e.g. passive transport (movement from higher to lower concentration, no energy needed), osmosis (diffusion of water across the membrane), facilitated diffusion (membrane proteins/channels provide a pathway for particles), active transport (movement against the concentration gradient using energy), or membrane-assisted transport (endocytosis, exocytosis, phagocytosis, pinocytosis, with vesicles).
Names a second distinct process from the list in P1, different from the first, and describes it correctly. Naming the same process twice, or a name with no description, earns no mark.

Names a third distinct process from the list in P1, different from the first two, and describes it correctly. Equivalent wording and other correct processes (such as pumps or channel proteins) also earn the mark.

rubric.notes: Award one mark for each different correct process that is both named and described accurately, up to three. Full marks need three distinct processes, each with a correct description; a name alone or a repeated process earns nothing. Equivalent wording and any correct process from the model answer are accepted.
